sentences.text: But it is undisputed that the petitioner has never availed or exercised his rights under Section 13 (2) of the PFA and that even in absence of manufacturer or dealer, the petitioner alone can be prosecuted and until and unless it is proved that the article was sold in the same conditions as he purchased it from license holder with a written warranty in prescribed form, he cannot claim exoneration from criminal liability.

5. Law is well settled that to assail the conviction on the ground of non-compliance of Section 13 (2)
of the Act, the accused/petitioner has to establish (i) that prejudice was caused to the defence, (ii)
that sample had deteriorated by the time the summons was received by the accused; and (iii) that the accused had utilised the right under Section 13 (2) of the Act, of sending the sample to the Director of Central Food Laboratory.

In this regard we can refer to Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram (AIR 1967 SC 970) (paragraph 4), Tulsiram v. State of Madhya Pradesh [(1984) 4 SCC 487], Prabhu v. State of Rajasthan [1994 Supp (2) SCC 177], T.V. Usman v. Food Inspector,
Tellicherry Municipality, Tellicherry [(1994) I SCC 754] and Gulab v. State of Madhya Pradesh [2008 (3) MPHT 131] (paragraphs 14 to 21).
6.

sentences.text: The Trial Court in paragraph 27 of the judgment observed that the accused failed to produce any proof that he purchased the clarified butter from license holder with a written warranty in prescribed form.

A photo-copy of the bill Ex. P-8 was handed over by the accused/petitioner to the complainant but the accused/petitioner failed to discharge the onus of proving the fact that this bill was issued by the concerned distributor.
Original bill was never produced or proved before the Trial Court.
The bill was not in the prescribed format VI-A read with Rule 12 A of the Rules.
Particulars given in the bill relied upon by the accused was not in accordance with the format.

The Trial Court observed that the article sold by the petitioner was not having any batch number or expiry date;
therefore, discarded photocopy of the bill (Ex. P-8) observing that it cannot be considered to be issued in consonance with Section 14 of the Act.
It is further observed that there is nothing to show that the clarified butter was sold in the same condition in which it had been purchased by the accused.
There is nothing to assail this finding of the Trial Court.

7. Thus, looking to the admitted position that the petitioner has never availed the right conferred under Section 13 (2) of the Act and there is nothing on record to show that conditions prescribed under Section 19 of the Act, 1954 have been complied with on grounds raised by the petitioner sentence cannot be suspended.
8.
The other ground taken by the petitioner is that this is a case of short sentence.

Out of six months,
the petitioner has served out 1 months six days sentence.
He is a small seller.

2 petition will take time.

sentences.text: The petitioner has never misused the liberty earlier granted to him by the trial Court.
Therefore, his sentence be suspended.
9. Looking to the evidence available on record and on these additional grounds also I am not inclined to suspend the sentence.
The same is accordingly declined.
10. However, liberty is granted to the petitioner, if he wishes to argue the matter finally at an early stage, he may move an application to that effect to show his willingness.
If such an application is filed, the matter may be listed immediately for consideration of the application.
Otherwise list this matter for final hearing in due course.
